validation: Don't add pruned blocks to m_blocks_unlinked on startup

LoadBlockIndex() adds to m_blocks_unlinked based only on nTx > 0, without
checking BLOCK_HAVE_DATA. Pruning preserves nTx but clears BLOCK_HAVE_DATA,
so a pruned block whose parent was header-only gets re-added on every
restart, causing the CheckBlockIndex() assertion that entries must have
data on disk to fail.

Check that BLOCK_HAVE_DATA is set before inserting into m_blocks_unlinked.

Fixes #35050.

Github-Pull: #35168

<!-- ralph-major:bitcoin/bitcoin -->

Ralph found major issues at 1bb872a8c83c643adc56eece18b7b0864bc9b91b.

**Prune request does not remove the stale-fork block file** (test/functional/feature_prune_stale_fork.py:30, head)

At height 500, the prune request is clamped to height 212 because pruning retains the last 288 blocks. In `-fastprune` mode, block files roll over at 64 KiB, and the small coinbase-only blocks do not fill the file containing the height-2 stale-fork child by height 212. Manual pruning removes only whole files whose last block height is within the prune limit, so the child remains available and the following `getblock` assertion fails before restart. Mine enough blocks for the child's file to become eligible for pruning, or otherwise ensure that file is pruned before asserting the error.

[Full report](https://review.fish.foo/traces/36662-1bb872a8c83c643adc56eece18b7b0864bc9b91b-1363-1.html)
The Ralph finding looks like nothing to me.

ACK 1bb872a8c83c643adc56eece18b7b0864bc9b91b

I think Ralph would maybe be right if the test's chain started from genesis and the fork was at the second block. But that's not the case for this test, as the fork happens at block 201.

C'mon Ralph...
